tagline: Browser-native handwriting recognition with every classifier built from first principles.
short_description: MNIST OCR in WebAssembly with four transparent classifiers—centroid, k-NN, perceptron, and a hand-written MLP—trained in a Web Worker and scored live.
long_description: ocr-livive-net is a browser-native optical character recognizer that hides nothing. Four classifiers are implemented from scratch in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly: nearest-centroid over ten mean digit images, k-NN (k=3) over the training set, a softmax perceptron trained with mini-batch SGD, and a 784-32-10 MLP with hand-written backprop. All four train in a Web Worker on 10,000 MNIST images and are scored on 1,000 held-out digits, reaching roughly 77%, 92%, 88%, and 93% respectively. Drawn input is normalized with MNIST's own preprocessing—integer grayscale, bounding box, box filter to 20x20, and center-of-mass placement in a 28x28 frame. There is no ML framework or cloud call; the arithmetic is inspectable end to end.
notes: Custom domain ocr.livive.net from CNAME; GitHub Pages deploys built pkg/ artifacts on every push to main. MNIST subsets are committed as raw .u8 files. No README claims for the ONNX path beyond src/onnx.rs; the four classifiers above are the documented benchmark.

how_to_play.title: 1. Draw a digit
how_to_play.body: Use the canvas to write a single digit. The stroke is converted to integer grayscale, cropped to its bounding box, downsampled to 20x20, and centered by mass in a 28x28 frame.

how_to_play.title: 2. Compare four classifiers
how_to_play.body: Centroid, k-NN, perceptron, and MLP each return a prediction with their own confidence. The live table shows how the simple baselines fail where the MLP succeeds.

how_to_play.title: 3. Train in the browser
how_to_play.body: Training runs in a Web Worker on committed MNIST subsets, so you can watch accuracy evolve and re-run the benchmark without a backend.
